description.narrative: 221. The socio-economic benefits created by the BGI IP through its country child projects will derive from interventions to address drivers of ecosystem degradation that reduce ecosystem services upon which local populations depend for livelihoods, income, food security, cultural services, etc. Although the GCP will not itself create socio-economic benefits, it will enhance the ability of the country child projects to do so through the strategic guidance, technical assistance and access to finance provided through the GCP’s Policy & Practice Facility and Nature Based Solutions Accelerator, as well as the knowledge products, tools and collaborative learning provided through the GCP’s Knowledge Management and Learning Cluster, including through the Regional Nodes and Thematic Working Groups overseen by the Cluster. 222. Through the IP / GCP monitoring and evaluation system (Outcome 3.2), the GCP will collate information from child projects and inform the BGI IP Advisory Board and the GCP Steering Committee on the socio-economic benefits generated by the GCP and the country child projects by tracking related program indicators, including:· Programme Level Indicator 1.1.1 Number of positive (economic) incentives developed, and negative incentives eliminated, to promote biodiversity conservation and sustainable use and NbS (aligned with GBF Target 18)· Programme Level Indicator: 1.3.1 Amount of US$ financing mobilized for NbS in key economic sectors (scaling up, scaling out & scaling deep) (aligned with GBF Target 19)· Programme Level Indicator: 2.1.3 % of the NbS investments that empower women participation (women hold senior management role, enterprise owned by women, women are >50% workforce, or products and services are specifically benefit women).· Programme Level Indicator: 2.2.1 % of beneficiaries and partners surveyed that report increased capacity to execute innovative NbS at seascape and landscape levels, disaggregated by sex, sector, youth, IP, vulnerable people · Programme Level Indicator: 2.4 Number of good practices and gender responsive lessons learned identified, documented and disseminated by the child project & GCP
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To empower collaboration, capacity and multistakeholder partnerships among BGI IP child projects to facilitate nature-positive development and reduce ecosystem degradation linked to the tourism, food and urban sectors in SIDS
